rule: One entry per URL, applied only to that URL. W2L still reads the host's robots.txt and records its verdict; the rule set aside, the reason and recordedBy appear in the trace, in a robots_overridden warning on the result and in the compliance record. An entry is added only for a file the publisher itself publishes, fetched once for citation; the check script and every run record keep the override visible.

overrides.reason: Equinix's own 2025 Data Summary, published on its AEM asset host; that host's robots.txt is a blanket Disallow: / for every crawler, not a statement about this report. One file, fetched once, to cite its figures.
Equinix's own green-finance document on the same AEM asset host (URL as the seed user recorded it, possibly truncated); the host's blanket Disallow: / addresses crawlers. One file, fetched once.
Equinix's own 2025 green bond allocation report on its AEM asset host, whose blanket Disallow: / addresses crawlers. One file, fetched once, to cite its figures.

Microsoft's own 2025 sustainability factsheet, published behind Microsoft's aka.ms short link; the short-link host's blanket Disallow: / addresses crawlers of the redirector, and W2L follows the redirect to the file once. The override names the short link only.

Google's own 2025 Environmental Report, published on gstatic.com, whose robots.txt allows only listed paths and ends with Disallow: /; the rule addresses crawlers, not this report. One file, fetched once, to cite its figures.

Digital Realty's own 2605 Impact Report, published on its marketing-platform host; that host's robots.txt Disallow: /rs/ is the platform's blanket rule for its asset path, addressed to crawlers, not a statement about this report (in the second run the host answered 404 to both the rule and the file). One file, fetched once, to cite its figures.
